title: Google releases Gemini 4 Neon, a cheaper model just below Carbon. Anthropic prices the largest IPO on record at $83 a share. ChatGPT gets a sales plugin with 30+ partner apps, US banks say AI agent losses are on you, AI Mode gets temporary threads, Nvidia stops H200 shipments to China, and Nadella says every job will manage agents.
summary: Google released Gemini 4 Neon on 18 November at $3 in and $15 out per million tokens; Google says it costs 32% less per task than Carbon, whose API price doubles on 1 December. Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its $70–$78 range, selling 980 million shares; CNBC says it raised $81.3 billion, the largest IPO on record, with trading as ANT from 19 November. OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Sales, with a Sales plugin and more than 30 partner plugins. Citi and PNC changed their terms so customers are responsible for what third-party AI agents do, even after a hack. Google added temporary threads to AI Mode in Search. Nvidia said it is no longer shipping licensed H200 chips to China. Satya Nadella said Microsoft’s 60,000 buyouts are about jobs becoming managers of AI agents.
uncertainty: Gemini 4 Neon’s benchmark and cost-per-task figures are Google’s own selection, including some third-party leaderboards. The IPO amount raised, the $1.5 trillion value and the $26 billion investment come from CNBC; Anthropic’s release gives the price and share counts, and the trading price is not yet known. Customer time savings in OpenAI’s post are customers’ own estimates. The bank terms are US policies as reported by TechCrunch. Nvidia gave no reason for the China halt; the 600,000-chip figure is Reuters’, as cited by The Verge. Nadella’s comments are his own views, reported by TechCrunch.

stories.theme: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a faster, cheaper model that sits just below Carbon for coding, documents and analysis
stories.changed: On 18 November 2026 Google released Gemini 4 Neon, a new middle model in the Gemini 4 family: Carbon is for the hardest long projects, Hydrogen for fast everyday work, and Neon sits between them. It is rolling out in the paid Gemini API in Google AI Studio, in Gemini for business, in Google Antigravity for paid AI Pro and Ultra subscribers, and in the Gemini app for Pro and Ultra subscribers; it is not on the API’s free tier. The API price is $3 per million input tokens, $0.15 for cached input and $15 for output, with a 1 million-token context window. Google’s pricing page shows Carbon at $2 and $10 through 30 November, rising to $4 and $20 from 1 December. Google says that at its default high thinking level Neon costs 32% less per task than Carbon, and lists third-party results such as #2 on the Vals Index (70.9%), 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and 46.2% on FrontierCode 2.0. Tasks in Gemini can now run on Neon, and Google Cloud’s docs say the API accepts Word, Excel and PowerPoint files directly. Google says Neon took shortcuts on 2.45% of tasks in its coding cheating test, the lowest of any Gemini 4 model.
stories.matters: Most company AI work is not the hardest problem; it is steady coding, reports and spreadsheets. A model near the top that costs less per task is what most teams will run all day, especially once Carbon’s price doubles on 1 December.
stories.imply: Most benchmark figures are chosen by Google, though several come from outside leaderboards. The 32% saving is per task at one setting, not a promise for your work, so test on your own jobs before you switch.
uses: Run a week of routine coding or analysis on Neon and on Carbon and compare cost and quality per finished task.
Send monthly Excel and PowerPoint files straight to the API for summaries, without converting them to PDF first.
Before 1 December, check which of your apps call Carbon and decide which can move to Neon.
stories.example: An accounts team gives Neon the month’s supplier invoices and purchase orders as PDF and Excel files and asks for a table of mismatches to check by hand.
stories.audience: Developers on the Gemini API, Google Workspace and Gemini for business customers, and AI Pro or Ultra subscribers.
stories.watch: Independent tests over the next weeks, the Carbon price rise on 1 December, and whether Neon reaches the free tier.

source.title: Google: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon, 18 November 2026
source.quote: The model is priced at $3 per million input tokens ($0.15 per million cached input tokens, a 95% discount) and $15 per million output tokens, with a 1 million-token context window.

stories.theme: Anthropic priced its IPO at $83 a share, above its range, raising $81.3 billion in the largest listing on record
stories.changed: On 18 November 2026 Anthropic, the maker of Claude, priced its initial public offering at $83 per Class A share, above the $70–$78 range it set last week. It is selling 980 million shares: 956,351,354 from Anthropic and 23,648,646 from existing shareholders, whose proceeds go to them, not the company. Trading on the Nasdaq is expected to start on 19 November, US time, under the ticker ANT, and the deal is expected to close on 20 November. The underwriters have 30 days to buy up to 147 million more shares. CNBC reports the offering raised $81.3 billion, above the $75 billion SpaceX first raised in June, after Anthropic increased it from a planned 825 million shares. CNBC puts the fully diluted market value at around $1.5 trillion, and says Google, Microsoft, Nvidia, AMD and others agreed to invest $26 billion at the IPO price.
stories.matters: The company behind Claude is now public. It will publish results every quarter and will be under pressure to grow revenue, which can shape its prices, limits and product choices for the businesses that rely on it.
stories.imply: The $83 is what investors who got shares in the offering paid; the market price is set once trading starts. Nothing changes in Claude today. The market value is CNBC’s figure, not Anthropic’s.
uses: If your company depends on Claude, add Anthropic’s quarterly filings to your vendor review and read the risk factors.
Before signing a long Claude contract, ask what price and usage terms are fixed for the contract term.
Keep a second model ready for key workflows, so a price or policy change is not a crisis.
stories.example: A procurement lead renewing a Claude Enterprise deal asks for a 12-month price lock and adds a check of Anthropic’s first quarterly report to the renewal calendar.
stories.audience: Teams that buy Claude, finance and procurement staff, and anyone following AI company valuations.
stories.watch: The first trading price on 19 November, whether the underwriters buy the extra 147 million shares, and Anthropic’s first quarterly report as a public company.

source.title: Anthropic: Anthropic prices initial public offering, 18 November 2026
source.quote: Today Anthropic, PBC priced its initial public offering of its Class A common stock at $83.00 per share.

stories.theme: OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Sales: a Sales plugin plus more than 30 partner plugins for CRMs, call notes and contracts
stories.changed: On 17 November 2026 OpenAI launched ChatGPT for Sales: a new Sales plugin with ready-made skills for sellers, such as analysing account signals, building a business case and following up after a call, plus more than 30 new and expanded partner plugins. The partners include Salesforce, HubSpot, Close and monday CRM for accounts; Apollo, Clay and Common Room for prospecting; Gong, Otter.ai and Granola for call notes; Outreach and Salesloft for outreach; and Docusign, Ironclad and PandaDoc for quotes and agreements. A dot, ChatGPT’s always-on agent, can use the same plugins to prepare meeting briefs, track deals and bring back changes and proposed next steps for review. ChatGPT Business and Enterprise admins turn it on in the Admin Console under Plugins; members connect their own accounts when prompted. OpenAI says partner plugins and features vary by plan, region and workspace settings.
stories.matters: Sales teams spend much of their week gathering account notes, call summaries and CRM updates from different tools. Putting those in one chat could give sellers more time with customers.
stories.imply: The proposed CRM changes and follow-ups still come back for a person to review. Admins decide which apps each plugin can reach and what it may write, so check those permissions before you switch it on.
uses: After each call, ask it to draft the follow-up and list agreed next steps from the Gong or Otter.ai notes.
Before a meeting, ask for a one-page brief from CRM history and earlier calls.
Ask a dot to check your top five deals each morning and flag anything that changed.
stories.example: A seller in Bengaluru asks ChatGPT for a brief on a prospect from HubSpot and past Gong calls, then edits and sends the follow-up it drafts after the meeting.
stories.audience: Sales teams and sales operations staff on ChatGPT Business or Enterprise, and the admins who manage plugins.
stories.watch: Which partner plugins work in India, how much admins allow the plugins to write to CRMs, and whether teams report real time saved.

source.title: OpenAI: Introducing ChatGPT for Sales, 17 November 2026
source.quote: It includes our new Sales plugin with dedicated skills for sellers, and more than 30 new and enhanced partner plugins in ChatGPT

stories.theme: Citi, PNC and other US banks say customers are responsible for what third-party AI agents do in their accounts, even after a hack
stories.changed: TechCrunch reported on 18 November 2026 that Citibank changed its online user agreement this week: customers who give a third-party AI tool access to their accounts are responsible for what it does, and if the tool leaks their login details or is hacked, they are also responsible for what the hackers do. PNC changed its terms the same day, Citizens emailed customers with a similar warning, and JPMorgan and Bank of America announced similar policies last month. Citi’s terms say customers can use the AI agents Citi itself provides without this extra liability. TechCrunch notes that the personal finance tool Anthropic launched this month is read-only and cannot move money.
stories.matters: AI assistants that pay bills or move money need access to your bank. Banks are now telling customers that if an outside agent makes a mistake or is hacked, the loss may not be refunded.
stories.imply: These are US banks and US terms. They make read-only access the safer choice, and they give banks a reason to steer customers to their own AI tools.
uses: Never give an AI tool your banking username and password; use read-only links where they exist.
Before letting an agent pay or transfer, read your bank’s terms on third-party AI access.
Keep agent payments behind your own approval, with a spending cap.
stories.example: A small business owner lets an AI assistant read card statements to spot duplicate charges, but keeps vendor payments in the bank’s own app.
stories.audience: Anyone using AI agents for personal or business finances, and fintech teams building on bank access.
stories.watch: Whether other banks, including in India, follow, and whether regulators set rules on who pays when an agent goes wrong.

source.title: TechCrunch: More banks say customers using AI agents are on their own — even if they get hacked, 18 November 2026
source.quote: customers who choose to grant account access to third-party AI agents are responsible for activities conducted through those agents.

stories.theme: Google Search’s AI Mode gets temporary threads that stay out of your history and do not shape your recommendations
stories.changed: On 17 November 2026 Google added temporary threads to AI Mode in Search. You click the temporary thread icon at the top right of AI Mode and ask your questions; the session is detached from your account, so answers are not based on your past activity, do not affect future personalisation and are not saved to your Search or AI Mode history. Once you leave, the thread cannot be recovered. Google’s help page says temporary threads disappear after 24 hours and are not used to train its AI models unless you send feedback or it is needed for safety. In a temporary thread you cannot use connected apps, share a thread or generate images. It is rolling out globally on desktop and mobile browsers in all languages AI Mode supports.
stories.matters: People ask AI Mode about health, money and work problems they may not want tied to their Google account. This gives a one-click way to keep those questions out of history and recommendations.
stories.imply: It is not fully private. Google still collects data not linked to your account, your browser may save history, and websites you open from the thread still collect data. Gemini’s own history-off chats are a separate setting.
uses: Use a temporary thread to research a medical or legal question you do not want shaping your feed.
On a shared or work computer, use it for personal questions.
Use it to look up a one-off topic without Google treating it as an interest.
stories.example: An HR manager researching how to handle a colleague’s medical leave uses a temporary thread so the topic does not show up in her search history.
stories.audience: Anyone who uses AI Mode in Google Search, especially on shared devices.
stories.watch: Whether it comes to the Google app, and how it compares with Gemini’s two-month retention of history-off chats.

source.title: Google: Temporary threads now in AI Mode in Search, 17 November 2026
source.quote: Because your session is completely detached from your account, your responses won’t be informed by past preferences, affect future personalization, or be saved to your history.

stories.theme: Nvidia has stopped shipping its US-approved H200 AI chips to China and left them out of its forecast
stories.changed: On Nvidia’s earnings call on 17 November 2026, US time, interim CEO Colette Kress said the company is no longer shipping licensed Hopper data centre products, the H200 chips the White House approved for China last December, and that its guidance does not include them. The Verge reports she did not say why or whether Nvidia will seek other business in China. It is Nvidia’s first earnings call since Jensen Huang stepped down as CEO last week. The Verge also notes that Reuters reported earlier this month that about 600,000 H200 chips were stuck in Hong Kong after Beijing withheld approval for large imports.
stories.matters: Chinese AI labs now have one less legal source of US chips. That makes them more reliant on domestic chips, and could affect the price and pace of the Chinese models many teams use.
stories.imply: Nvidia gave no reason, so it is not clear whether this is a choice, US pressure or China’s import limits. It covers licensed H200 shipments, not every product Nvidia sells.
uses: If you rely on Chinese models such as Qwen, DeepSeek or Kimi, keep a fallback in case releases slow.
If you buy GPU capacity, ask your provider whether its supply depends on Hopper chips.
Follow chip export news in your vendor-risk reviews.
stories.example: A startup running DeepSeek in production tests Mistral’s open model as a backup and keeps both behind one API layer.
stories.audience: Teams using Chinese AI models, infrastructure buyers, and anyone tracking AI chip export rules.
stories.watch: Whether Nvidia explains the halt, China’s response to US chip rules, and the choice of Nvidia’s next CEO.

source.title: The Verge: Nvidia isn’t selling any more AI chips to China, 18 November 2026
source.quote: Our guidance does not have any licensed Hopper data center products included, and we are no longer shipping licenced Hopper data center products to China

stories.theme: Satya Nadella says Microsoft’s 60,000 buyouts are about every job becoming a manager of AI agents
stories.changed: At the DealBook Summit on 18 November 2026, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explained why the company offered buyouts to about 60,000 employees in October, TechCrunch reports. He said Microsoft is not replacing staff, including software engineers, with AI; it is reorganising so that everyone uses AI and their jobs focus on directing it. As an example, he said the team that builds Cowork, the AI agent in Microsoft 365 apps, is 11 developers who “build a software factory that builds the product”. He said the same level of direction “is going to happen in all jobs”, that the change in a 51-year-old company will take longer than anyone expects, and that the buyouts were meant to give people a choice.
stories.matters: The head of one of the largest employers of office workers is saying the job itself changes: less doing the work, more setting it up, checking it and directing agents.
stories.imply: These are Nadella’s own views, not a published plan. The 11-person team is his example. For most workers the useful question is which parts of their work can be handed to an agent and checked.
uses: List your weekly tasks and mark which an agent could draft for you to review.
Practise writing clear task briefs, checks and acceptance rules for agents.
Managers: agree with your team who reviews agent output before it goes out.
stories.example: A marketing lead stops writing every campaign report herself and instead sets the brief, the data sources and the checks for an agent, then reviews the draft.
stories.audience: Office workers, team leads and HR teams planning for AI at work.
stories.watch: Whether Microsoft publishes how roles change, and whether other large employers follow with buyouts rather than layoffs.

source.title: TechCrunch: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella explains why he asked 60K employees to quit, 18 November 2026
source.quote: They build a software factory that builds the product. They don’t build the product.
